subject: How to profile a model to determine it's "category"?

messages.author: c2d1891042fbb9d5
messages.subject: How to profile a model to determine it's "category"?
parts:
Hello,

I'm working to try and find out if a model some researchers I work with can be optimized. Having read through several issues on the adcomp tracker I located this comment

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/122#issuecomment-159552952

Notably on page 16 there is a table explaining how models are processing time in AD, outside AD (Cholesky factorization/Inverse subset)  in R GC/other.

Does anyone know how to begin to determine these numbers for a model? TMB::benchmark seems to provide details on Cholesky factorization and how parallelization affects it but is there some other utility I cannot find that provides the time spent in the various parts of the algorithm?

Thank you very much,

Mike

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: How to profile a model to determine it's "category"?
parts:
Profiling from R may give you some useful information:

Rprof(); obj$fn(); Rprof(NULL)
summaryRprof()

Rprof(); obj$gr(); Rprof(NULL)
summaryRprof()

Look for 'updateCholesky' and 'solveSubset'...
